item.title: FCC Cutting Satellite Approval Lag In Half, Chairman Says
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission has reduced by half the backlog of satellite application approvals as it broadly seeks to stimulate the space and communications economy, Chairman Brendan Carr said in an interview on Bloomberg TV.

item.title: Zurich Ranks Top in Disposable Income Poll Despite $7 Coffees
item.description: Zurich and Geneva may be the most expensive places in the world to buy your meat and veg but it’ll still pay off as the two Swiss cities top a new survey of the highest disposable incomes in the world.

item.title: Apollo’s Slok Warns of Dollar’s Vulnerability to an AI Pullback
item.description: The dollar’s recent gains are at risk if the selloff in artificial intelligence stocks deepens, according to Apollo Global Management Inc.’s Torsten Slok.

item.title: Sunrun Offers Solar Users Hundreds Per Month in Compute Program
item.description: Sunrun Inc. is piloting a program aimed at enabling customers to earn hundreds of dollars per month that would use electricity from rooftop solar installations to power distributed computing, according to Chief Executive Officer Mary Powell.

item.title: American Aid Worker With Ebola ‘Stable’ in German Hospital
item.description: An American aid worker who tested positive for Ebola is stable and being treated in a specialized isolation unit at Frankfurt University Hospital in Germany, according to a statement from the hospital.

item.title: Millennium Taps JPMorgan Veteran to Lead New Push Into Brazil
item.description: Billionaire Izzy Englander’s Millennium Management is expanding into Latin America’s biggest economy.

item.title: Trump Says US Will Be Reimbursed 20% Rate for Hormuz Traffic
item.description: President Donald Trump said the US would reinstate its blockade of Iranian ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and demanded a 20% reimbursement on all other cargo shipped through the waterway.

item.title: London IPO Revival Faces Setback as Hopefuls Consider Delays
item.description: Several UK companies including Waterstones Booksellers Ltd. and SumUp Payments Ltd. are considering deferring their initial public offerings in London to 2027, according to people familiar with the matter, denting the capital’s hopes for a substantial revival in listings activity this year.

item.title: Switzerland and UK Agree Trade Deal to Deepen Post-Brexit Ties
item.description: Switzerland and the UK concluded talks on an updated free-trade agreement, bringing Western Europe’s two major non-European Union economies closer together with a pact focused on services.

item.title: India Pushes State Banks to Step Up Foreign Currency Deposits
item.description: India has asked state-owned banks to intensify efforts to garner foreign currency deposits from the 35-million-strong diaspora, as the country seeks to boost its external buffers and shore up the flagging rupee.

item.title: Cocoa’s Uneven Demand Recovery Runs Into Fresh Price Volatility
item.description: Cocoa demand is expected to remain uneven across the world, suggesting the recovery remains fragile as renewed supply concerns push bean prices higher and threaten to keep chocolate pricier for longer.

item.title: Apple’s Lawsuit Threatens to Disrupt OpenAI’s Bid to Rival the iPhone
item.description: Apple Inc.’s lawsuit accusing OpenAI of systematically stealing its intellectual property threatens to disrupt the AI company’s device ambitions long before the case is resolved.

item.title: Kenya Eyes $500 Million Eurobond Buyback to Ease Debt Pressure
item.description: Kenya is considering buying back as much as $500 million of its eurobonds to extend maturities and ease repayment pressures, according to people familiar with the plans.

item.title: US Stocks Fall as Mideast Tensions Flare Anew, Oil Climbs
item.description: US stocks dropped on Monday as investors assessed tit-for-tat attacks between the US and Iran and conflicting information over the status of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Ethiopian Central Bank Raises Rates for First Time in Two Years
item.description: Ethiopia’s central bank raised the nation’s benchmark interest rate for the first time since its introduction two years ago to rein in inflation as it removed a cap on credit growth.

item.title: StanChart Sees Slower Nigeria Rate Cuts as Inflation Views Rise
item.description: Standard Chartered Plc. said that the Central Bank of Nigeria’s easing cycle will likely be slower and more cautious as inflation will be higher than anticipated and expectations remain unanchored.

item.title: Intel Invests €5 Billion in Irish Hub to Keep Up in AI Chip Race
item.description: Intel Corp. is spending €5 billion ($5.7 billion) to expand its plant in Ireland, as the chipmaker attempts to regain its manufacturing dominance for the AI boom.

item.title: Bangladesh Is a Nuclear Power Test Case for Developing Nations
item.description: Atomic energy offers emerging economies a way to wean themselves off imported fossil fuels, but it also has downsides.

item.title: Saudi Energy Minister’s Influence Grows With Industry Portfolio
item.description: Saudi Arabian Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman was appointed minister of industry and mineral resources in addition to his current post, signaling an expanded role for the royal and closer integration of the two sectors.

item.title: Renewed Iran Woes Flip Script for Traders Betting War Risks Over
item.description: A day after making an investment call tied to subsiding Middle East tensions, BCA Research’s Marko Papic had to scrap his recommendation at a loss. Donald Trump had said the war in Iran was back on.

item.title: ChatGPT’s Upgraded Voice Mode Captures the Imperfections of Real Conversations
item.description: The OpenAI chatbot now speaks and converses a lot more like a real person

item.title: Washington Is Looking to Keep China From Training Its AI on US Models
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI’s warnings about “adversarial distillation” are reinvigorating one of the oldest debates in Silicon Valley.

item.title: A Summer Reading List to Grasp the Geopolitical Shifts Shaping the Future
item.description: US Treasury’s Bessent lays out a ‘doctrine’ steeped in economic self-reliance

item.title: Why Global Economy’s Resilience May Rise With Diminished Dollar Dominance
item.description: The decline in the dollar’s role reduces ripples of stress through the world in times of crisis

item.title: Chile Debt Sale Window Opens as Investors Ignore Mounting Risks
item.description: Chile’s government has a window of opportunity to sell debt abroad as sovereign spreads hover near two-decade lows, with investors shrugging off an escalation in the Middle East conflict, domestic debt woes and a stagnating economy.

item.title: US Cost for Gas Power at 17-Year High and Climbing, Lazard Says
item.description: The cost of power from natural gas-fired plants in the US hit the highest level in at least 17 years, and is poised to climb even higher as demand surges from new data centers.

item.title: India Inflation Tops RBI Target for First Time in 17 Months
item.description: India’s inflation accelerated last month, rising above the Reserve Bank of India’s target for the first time in nearly a year and a half and keeping policymakers on guard.

item.title: Researchers Raise Concerns That AI May Atrophy Human Skills
item.description: Will we end up with a generation of experts in high-stakes professions who never build true expertise?

item.title: Investors Expect ‘Sunshine and Rainbows’ This Earnings Season
item.description: Estimates are running up against sticky inflation and rising odds of interest rate hikes. With stocks near records, there’s little room for error.

item.title: Apple’s $600 Billion Rally Fueled by Traders Fleeing AI Selloff
item.description: Investors are flocking back to Apple Inc. as nervousness about artificial intelligence spending weighs on the stocks of chipmakers and cloud-computing giants.
